keeper_snapshot.definition: KEEPER. neiso-99 arm B, the JOINT arm: it settles BOTH standing NEISO owner escalations in ONE re-solve so they are not confounded (ASSESSMENT-neiso98 §4.1/§4.2). (1) AUDIT ROW O5 — the recipe moves off the ARCHIVED P2 commitment pass onto the production P1 basis; NEISO was the only keeper of six that ran, and was RENDERED FROM, P2, so every published NEISO number sat on a pass CLAUDE.md says no keeper uses. This bundle persists ['P1'] alone. (2) THE STONY BROOK ROUTING DEFECT — _resolve_unit_group's fac_group short-circuit handed a liquid-fuel combustion turbine's outage window to a sibling GAS bin, so plant 6081's two Diesel Oil CTs (83 MW each, 74 windows each) derated a 305.1 MW combined cycle they are not in for 48.7% of the 2024 and 56.0% of the 2025 capacity-year — years in which the CC units 001/002/003 have NO windows of their own at all. Three more NEISO plants were affected (1595 Kendall S6, 568 Bridgeport BHB4, 1588 Mystic MJ-1). Rule 14 [R-ACCURATE]. DETERMINATION CALIBRATED (rubric v3.3, owner amendment 2026-08-17: a ledgered C3c caveat is REPORTED at full magnitude but no longer DOWNGRADES the determination; before the amendment this run read the with-caveats determination, and no criterion moved), criterion for criterion IDENTICAL to the superseded keeper — 0 FAILs, C3c the sole ledgered caveat, C1 all 12/12 free 8/8, grade scored 8 / target 7 / commercial 0 / ledgered 1 — so NO GATE WAS TRADED for the two corrections, and rule 22 D-5(b)'s worse-determination stop does not fire. THE MOVEMENT IS DECOMPOSED, NOT CONFLATED, against the same-HEAD basis-only control 2026-08-17-neiso-99-basis-p1: the basis leg is a pure re-render (bit-identical to the incumbent's own P1, 0 differing cells every year) worth mean lambda -0.0575 / -0.0110 / -0.0378 and the 2024 annual max $256.93 -> $218.24; the routing leg is worth a further -0.0162 / -0.0133 / -0.1112 $/MWh with the annual maxima unmoved. ONE PREREG EXPECTATION IS REFUTED AND SAID SO: the routing arm's dispatch effect is dominated by KENDALL, not Stony Brook — restoring 6081's availability barely moves its dispatch because that block's heat rate 10.6062 sits above 97.5% of NEISO's CC_REGULAR capacity (cap-weighted p50 7.340), i.e. it is deep out of merit whether or not it is available, the same fact neiso-83 measured at the same plant. Frontier re-verified on THIS keeper's own sidecars (probe neiso99_declaration_recheck): C3c model tail 0 h > $300/MWh in all three years on the now-sole P1 pass, agreeing with the payload's ordc.hoursGt200.model 0/0/0 vs RT actuals 15/8/20, closest approach $280.85 (short by $19.15); the RCPF co-optimization DORMANT in all 78,840 family-hours at the published statics (1,800/1,200/600 MW) with |dual| max EXACTLY 0.0 — the prior keeper's 1.42e-14 degeneracy noise left with the P2 pass.
